slides.h1: The Investing Mistake That Never Looks Like One
slides.sub: Impulsive high-conviction bets, sized far too large — Mars bias.

slides.body: A fast, decisive entry — sized like a sure thing. Mars gives conviction and speed. It never provides position-sizing discipline.

slides.h2: Why it feels right in the moment
slides.body: Mars-driven decisions come with genuine confidence, not recklessness-that-feels-reckless. That's exactly what makes the oversized bet hard to catch in real time.

slides.h2: The house that keeps it honest
slides.body: The 11th house (gains) shows what you actually keep. A brilliant call sized too large can still net out worse than a smaller, repeatable one.
It's separating conviction (a Mars strength, keep it) from sizing (a discipline, build it deliberately — Mars won't supply this on its own).
A free wealth-psychology read shows which bias shows up most in your chart.
